_about: Real decisions where a person did not get the free legal aid they were entitled to (Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, Art. 39A / 21 of the Constitution, s.304 CrPC) and that weighed in the decision. Every field comes from the decision text saved in sources/<doc>.txt; null means the decision does not say it. 'replay' is ours: the answers the person could give on the app's screens using only facts the decision states (poverty without an income figure is 'unsure', never 'yes'), what rules.js returns, and the Section 12 clause(s) matching the reason the court gave (court_clauses, empty when the court rested on the right of every unrepresented accused). 'excluded' are decisions read in full and left out, with why. Collected from indiankanoon.org on 2026-11-05.

cases.person: Hussainara Khatoon and others (undertrial prisoners in Bihar jails, e.g. Budhu Mahli, Ranchi Central Jail)

facts_where.custody: 'Budhu Mahli ... has been in jail since 21st November, 1972'
facts_where.poor: 'on account of their poverty, they are unable to engage a lawyer who would apprise them of their right to apply for bail'

cases.time_lost: Budhu Mahli in jail as undertrial since 21 Nov 1972 (over six years); others since 1974; some longer than maximum sentence
cases.outcome: undertrials held beyond maximum sentence released; State directed to provide lawyer at own cost at next remand for bail; legal aid read into Art. 21
court_relied_on: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
M.H. Hoskot v. State of Maharashtra
cases.quote: It is not uncommon to find that under-trial prisoners who are produced before the Magistrates are unaware of their right to obtain release on bail and on account of their poverty, they are unable to engage a lawyer who would apprise them of their right to apply for bail
cases.limits: Systemic order over thousands of undertrials; no number of people without a lawyer is stated, so persons_count null. Closer to a PIL but names individual prisoners and orders relief for them.

replay.court_basis: undertrials held in jail who, being poor, had no lawyer to apply for bail

cases.person: Khatri and others (the Bhagalpur blinded prisoners, undertrials; e.g. Umesh Yadav)

facts_where.disability: 'the blinded prisoners ... their vision is so totally impaired that it is not possible to restore it'
facts_where.custody: 'the rest of them continued to languish in jail'; Bhagalpur Central Jail
facts_where.poor: Umesh Yadav petition: 'since he had no money to prosecute this police officer, he should be provided a lawyer at Government expense'

cases.what_was_missing: not told of the right; no lawyer at first production and remand
cases.time_lost: most remained in jail; a few released on bail 'after being in jail for quite some time'
cases.outcome: interim order: magistrates directed to inform every indigent accused of right to free legal aid; State told aid starts at first production; petition adjourned
court_relied_on: Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar
cases.quote: The records of the judicial magistrates show that no legal representation was provided to the blinded prisoners, because none of them asked for it nor did the judicial magistrates enquire from the blinded prisoners produced before them either initially or at the time of remand whether they wanted any legal representation at State cost.
cases.limits: Group case; text says 'most of the blinded prisoners' were unrepresented without giving a number. Separately, Umesh Yadav and 'Ten other blinded prisoners' (11) asked for a State lawyer to prosecute the police and the Sessions Judge said there was no provision; persons_count left null because the main group size is not stated. Interim order, individual relief deferred to a later hearing.

replay.court_basis: indigent accused produced before the magistrate from jail, never asked whether they wanted a lawyer at State cost

cases.person: Suk Das (appellant, accused convicted under s.506/34 IPC)

facts_where.poor: he was admittedly unable to afford legal representation on account of his poverty

cases.what_was_missing: not told of the right; no lawyer at trial
cases.time_lost: was in jail nearly 8 months (sentence reduced by High Court to period undergone)
cases.outcome: conviction and sentence set aside; dismissal from service quashed, reinstatement without back wages; no fresh trial
cases.quote: It is obvious that in the present case the learned Additional Deputy Commissioner did not inform the appellant that he was entitled to free legal assistance nor did he inquire from the appellant whether he wanted a lawyer to be provided to them at State cost.
cases.limits: Title has two appellants ('Suk Das & Anr') but the judgment discusses only 'the appellant' (singular); counted 1. Relies on Hussainara Khatoon, M.H. Hoskot and Khatri (II). High Court had refused relief because no legal-aid application was made.

replay.court_basis: unable to afford a lawyer on account of his poverty, never told of free legal aid
replay.divergence: The decision gives poverty but no income figure, so the honest answer is "unsure": the app does not say eligible, it shows the State ceiling and sends him to the DLSA or 15100 (note_income_unsure). Custody during the trial is not stated (he was in jail about 8 months by the time of the High Court appeal).

cases.person: Mohd. Hussain @ Julfikar Ali (appellant, accused sentenced to death; Pakistani national)

facts_where.custody: the appellant was arrested in 1998 and since then he is in judicial custody

cases.what_was_missing: lawyer too late, no meaningful defence at trial
cases.outcome: conviction and death sentence set aside; de novo trial ordered from prosecution evidence stage, within three months, with counsel
cases.quote: the appellant was denied the assistance of a counsel in substantial and meaningful manner in the course of trial although necessity of counsel was vital and imperative and that resulted in denial of due process of law.
cases.limits: Three-judge bench answering a reference after split two-judge bench (Dattu J. remand; Prasad J. no retrial, deportation); both had held trial vitiated for lack of counsel. Larger bench ordered retrial despite delay.

replay.court_basis: the right of every accused to a counsel at State cost (Art. 21, 22(1), s.304 CrPC), whatever the category
replay.divergence: The app says eligible under (g), custody. The Court did not tie the right to a Section 12 category: it rests on the right of every unrepresented accused to counsel (s.304 CrPC, Art. 21). The failure was a lawyer named too late, which the app cannot fix; it only gets the application in early.

cases.person: Rajoo @ Ramakant (appellant, convict in gang-rape case)
cases.what_was_missing: High Court never asked if he wanted legal aid on appeal
cases.outcome: High Court judgment set aside; appeal remitted for fresh hearing after giving opportunity of legal representation
cases.quote: We are also of the view that the High Court was under an obligation to enquire from Rajoo whether he required legal assistance and if he did, it should have been provided to him at State expense.
cases.limits: Custody and means of the appellant not stated. Establishes that legal aid applies at appellate stage too.

replay.court_basis: Section 12 makes no distinction between trial and appeal for an accused or a person in custody
replay.divergence: The decision does not state his custody or income, so from the stated facts alone the app says not eligible and points to the DLSA. The Court read Section 12 as covering him as an accused/person in custody on appeal; a convict serving 10 years would answer custody "yes", but the text does not say it.

facts_where.custody: Accused Anokhilal present from judicial custody.

cases.what_was_missing: legal aid counsel named the day charges were framed; no time to prepare
cases.outcome: conviction and death sentence set aside; de novo consideration ordered; norms for legal-aid counsel laid down
cases.quote: In the process, the assistance that the appellant was entitled to in the form of legal aid, could not be real and meaningful.
cases.limits: Legal-aid counsel appointed the same day charges were framed; 13 witnesses examined in 7 days; trial over in under a month. Court expressly did not comment on merits.

replay.court_basis: legal aid must be real and meaningful (Art. 21, 39A); the Court laid down minimum experience and time
replay.divergence: The app says eligible under (g), custody. The Court did not rest on a category: he had a legal aid lawyer, but too late to prepare. The app cannot fix the quality of the lawyer.

cases.person: Ashok (appellant, accused sentenced to death, commuted to life by High Court)

facts_where.custody: the appellant had been incarcerated for about twelve years and nine months before he was released on bail

cases.what_was_missing: no lawyer at charge and examination-in-chief of the main witness
cases.time_lost: incarcerated about twelve years and nine months
cases.outcome: acquitted (on s.313 CrPC and evidence grounds); directions on legal aid to all State Legal Services Authorities
cases.quote: We are surprised to note that the examination-in-chief of PW-1 was allowed to be recorded without giving legal aid counsel to the appellant, who was not represented by an advocate.
cases.limits: Acquittal rests on failure to put incriminating material under s.313 CrPC and weak evidence; legal-aid failure (no lawyer at charge/PW-1 chief, absent legal aid advocate, poor cross-examination) produced the general directions in para 23 rather than being the sole ground. Victim was an SC child; appellant's own caste not stated.

replay.court_basis: the duty of the court to give legal aid counsel to an unrepresented accused (Art. 21, 39A)
replay.divergence: The app says eligible under (g), custody. The Court did not tie the right to a category. Acquittal rested mainly on s.313 CrPC and weak evidence; the legal aid failure led to directions to all State Legal Services Authorities.

cases.person: Sovaran Singh Prajapati (appellant, convict sentenced to death)

facts_where.custody: order 01.09.2015: 'Accused Sobran Singh present from jail in judiciary custody'
facts_where.poor: para 12(g): 'The accused being a person of considerably less means, did not have access to an independent counsel'

cases.what_was_missing: witnesses examined without counsel; legal aid counsel late and changed repeatedly
cases.time_lost: trial over 2.3 years (2014-2017), death sentence until 2025
cases.outcome: conviction and death sentence set aside; remanded for fresh trial from framing of charge
cases.quote: (d) The Legal Aid Counsel provided to the appellant was not only appointed at a belated stage but also changed more than once during the course of trial.
cases.limits: Also other lapses (Section 313 statement, delayed charge, Section 311 rejection) contributed to remand.

replay.court_basis: a person of considerably less means who had no access to an independent counsel
replay.divergence: The app says eligible under (g), custody; the Court pointed to his lack of means (h), which the app leaves to the DLSA as "unsure" without an income figure. Same result, different clause.

cases.person: Tarun Sharma (appellant, convict serving life imprisonment)

facts_where.custody: para 67: 'He is in custody and shall be released from prison forthwith'

cases.what_was_missing: amicus named and appeal heard the same day, no records, no time
cases.outcome: High Court and trial court judgments set aside; appellant acquitted on merits and released
court_relied_on: Mohd. Sukur Ali v. State of Assam
cases.quote: The appointed amicus was neither furnished with the case records from the lower Court nor afforded reasonable time to prepare the matter or consult with the accused-appellant.
cases.limits: SC held the High Court's procedure unfair but, given long incarceration, decided merits itself instead of remitting; acquittal rests on weak dying declaration. Own counsel was engaged but absent; amicus appointed.

replay.court_basis: a fair hearing of the appeal needs a counsel with time and records (Art. 21)
replay.divergence: The app says eligible under (g), custody. The Court did not tie the right to a category; the failure was a same-day amicus, which the app cannot fix. The Supreme Court acquitted him on the merits.

facts_where.custody: para 21: 'the accused, who was in jail and defended by a counsel from legal aid'

cases.what_was_missing: legal aid counsel named the day of the charge-sheet; charges framed next day
cases.time_lost: trial completed in 15 days (27.04.2018 to 12.05.2018); death sentence until 2023
cases.outcome: conviction and death sentence set aside; de novo trial; DLSA Indore to provide senior counsel
cases.quote: The Order-sheet would thus clearly indicate that the trial was conducted in a hurried manner without providing ample and proper opportunity to the defence counsel, who was engaged through legal aid, to prepare himself effectively.
cases.limits: Legal aid lawyer appointed same day as charge-sheet and charges framed next day; DNA/FSL reports also not proved.

replay.court_basis: Anokhilal norms: legal aid counsel must have time and experience (Art. 21, 39A)
replay.divergence: The app says eligible under (g), custody. The Court did not tie the right to a category; the failure was the time given to the lawyer, which the app cannot fix.

cases.person: Rafique, Nazim, Rahis, Azmal @ Aslam, Maksud Ahmed (appellants/accused)
cases.what_was_missing: six prosecution witnesses examined with no counsel and no legal aid substitute
cases.outcome: conviction (s.394/397/120-B IPC) set aside; retrial from prosecution evidence stage; legal aid/amicus to be provided if needed
cases.quote: The appellants were convicted by the trial court without providing an opportunity to be represented by their counsels or by providing legal aid counsel if their counsels were not available at the relevant time and without these said six witnesses being cross-examined.
cases.limits: Appellants had private counsel who were absent; failure was court not substituting legal aid counsel / denying cross-examination. Appellants were on bail; poverty not stated. Order circulated to all judicial officers.

replay.court_basis: the court must give legal aid counsel when the accused is unrepresented (Art. 21, 22(1), 39A)
replay.divergence: All five were on bail and the decision states no category or income, so from the stated facts the app says not eligible and points to the DLSA. The High Court rested on the duty of the trial court to every unrepresented accused, broader than the Section 12 categories the app asks about.

cases.case_number: CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 17912 of 2019 (with 9 connected bail applications)

facts_where.custody: para 6(a): "The applicant was in jail since 14.02.2008."
facts_where.poor: para 15: "The applicant is a financially destitute person belonging to a marginalized section of the society."

cases.what_was_missing: no legal aid to apply for bail for over a decade
cases.time_lost: in jail since 14.02.2008; bail heard on merits only 16.07.2022 (14.5 years)
cases.outcome: bail granted (interim made absolute); Charter of Prisoners' Rights and directions to magistrates, DLSAs, jail authorities, State
cases.quote: The accumulation of these circumstances of want paired with legal illiteracy and denial of legal aid prolonged the detention of the applicant and has led to a miscarriage of justice.
cases.limits: Order in this file decides only Ramu's bail; 9 companion applicants (Kamil, Muneesh, Mumtaj, Vinesh, Titu, Mintu, Saleem, Pramod Kumar, Sunil Kumar) and ~60 exemplar prisoners in para 17 table described with similar delays, not counted. Bail grounds on merits also listed (para 157). Sureties reduced earlier due to 'penurious condition and social exclusion' (para 8).

replay.court_basis: a financially destitute prisoner left in jail without legal aid for bail

cases.limits: Counsel (private or legal aid, unclear) on record but absent/refused; court held sham representation attracts s.304(1). Custody at trial not stated (appeal filed from District Jail, Meerut).

replay.court_basis: a man of no education and no means, never offered a lawyer at State expense
replay.divergence: The decision gives poverty but no income figure and does not say he was in custody during the trial (only that the appeal was filed from jail), so the app answers "unsure" and sends him to the DLSA instead of saying eligible.

facts_where.custody: para 22: 'Accused- Manglu is present in the court in Judicial Custody with his learned counsel Sri None'
facts_where.poor: para 25: 'the appellant had informed the court that he is very poor and could not afford any counsel'

cases.person: Govindaraju @ Kutti (appellant/accused, aged about 22, convicted under s.376 IPC and POCSO)
cases.what_was_missing: private counsel absent; cross-examination closed as nil without a legal aid counsel
cases.outcome: conviction and life sentence set aside; remanded for cross-examination of all prosecution witnesses with Legal Services Authority advocate if needed; circular to all district judges
court_relied_on: Ashok Debbarma v. State of Tripura
Rajaram Prasad Yadav v. State of Bihar
cases.quote: But, the fact remains that the trial Court has erred in not affording an opportunity to the accused to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses by providing free legal assistance.
cases.limits: Accused had a private lawyer who stopped appearing; not a case of initial denial of legal aid. Text does not state custody or poverty of this accused. Victim was a minor girl (child facts concern the victim, not the person denied aid).

replay.court_basis: the trial court must give a Legal Services Authority advocate when the accused is unrepresented (Art. 21, 22(1), 39A, s.304 CrPC)
replay.divergence: The decision states neither custody during the trial nor income, so the app has nothing to go on and says not eligible. The Court rested on the duty to every unrepresented accused, not on a Section 12 category.
